absent: Population, update and lifetime rules for syscall metadata tables and enter field lists.
Registration, enablement, locking and trigger semantics for trace events, tracepoints and perf probes.
Perf counting, sampling, branch stack and register capture behavior beyond identifier values.
Full field layout and version compatibility rules for the performance attribute structure beyond size milestones.
Print format consumption, iterator sequencing and error handling beyond delegation to generic helpers.

findings.text: Syscall tracing metadata carries a name pointer, numeric identifier, packed seven bit argument count plus one bit string marker, signed user argument size, short user mask, pointers to type and argument name tables, an embedded enter fields list, and separate enter and exit event call pointers.

One configuration mirrors a global syscall tracepoint work flag into a given task by setting the task flag when the global flag is set and clearing it otherwise. An alternate configuration is a no operation that leaves the task unchanged.

The tracing headers expose a family of definition helpers that turn a name plus prototype, arguments, layout, assignment and print descriptors into a reusable class and a concrete event. Variants add registration hooks, conditional gating, flag and perf permission annotations, and syscall specialization.
One helper builds a print descriptor by quoting the supplied format and appending a stringified argument list. A system alias forwards to the active trace system name.

Each event class produces a raw record beginning with a generic entry header followed by class specific fields and a trailing variable data area. Companion artifacts provide an offsets only structure, a fields table closed by an empty entry, an offsets measurer returning total variable size, and class plus call descriptors linked to tracepoint, print format and output helpers.

Emission checks for a soft disabled destination and returns early, measures variable payload size, reserves fixed plus variable space and returns early when reservation fails, instantiates field layout and assignment, then commits the buffer.
Event probes run under a non tracing preempt guard. The syscall specialized probe additionally marks a possible fault before taking the same guard, while the generic probe takes the guard directly.

Raw output prepares the iterator, verifies that the stored entry type matches the expected call type with a one time warning and unhandled return on mismatch, initializes a temporary sequence where needed, and delegates to generic print and return handling.

Class registration wires system name, fields array, raw initialization, probe and regular registration plus optional perf and BTF hooks. Each call is marked as a tracepoint, points at its class, output functions and print format, and is placed on a dedicated event section with four byte alignment.

Perf and BTF support is two state. Enabled stages declare a per call perf probe and a BTF identifier list for the trace function and raw record and install them into the class. Disabled stages expand to nothing, as do empty stages for flags, permissions and event definitions.

Syscall event classes reuse the generic class definition in most stages, with only the probe wrapper differing by fault handling. A compile time probe check validates that the template raw handler matches the expected callback type for the call.

Performance type space uses values zero through five for hardware, software, tracepoint, cache, raw and breakpoint with a non ABI max. PMU type shift is thirty two with a low thirty two bit hardware event mask. Generalized hardware counts span zero through nine, cache kinds zero through six with operation kinds zero through two and result kinds zero through one, and software counts zero through eleven, each followed by a non ABI max.

Sample selection uses single bit flags occupying bits zero through twenty four with bit twenty five as non ABI max, plus a combined weight selector covering two of those bits. Branch filtering uses shift positions zero through nineteen with matching single bit values and a combined privilege mask, branch shape codes zero through fifteen, speculation codes zero through three, fault and architecture codes zero through seven, privilege codes zero through three, and ARM64 aliases mapped onto the architecture codes.

Register ABI uses zero for none, one for thirty two bit and two for sixty four bit. Transaction flags use low bits zero through seven with bit eight as non ABI max and a high thirty two bit abort code field starting at bit thirty two. Read format uses bits zero through four with bit five as non ABI max. Published attribute sizes grow across ten versions from sixty four bytes to one hundred forty four bytes.
Two silent drop paths exist: a soft disabled destination returns without recording, and a failed buffer reservation returns without recording, so callers cannot assume an event was stored.
